The answer depends on the exact format of the XML you are using. You are right that there are multiple ways of specifying a tag, so I can't be sure about this example, but it should work if you try:

    <item>
        <title><![CDATA[Title]]></title>
    </item>

or

    <item>
        <title><![CDATA[Title]]></title>
    </item>

You should also use a `CDATA` block to prevent the XML from being treated as markup.

See also:

* [CDATA in XML](https://www.w3.org/MarkUp/taginfo/tdfa/CDATA) at the W3C taginfo project
* [CDATA Sections - HTML vs XML](https://www.w3.org/TR/html-markup/cdata-sections.html) at the HTML5 specification
* [CDATA in XML](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTML/Element/cdata-section) at the MDN web docs

Which of the following is the primary purpose of an audit?
A. To determine if the organization's financial statements are prepared in accordance with generally accepted accounting principles
B. To evaluate the organization's compliance with applicable laws, regulations, and contractual obligations
C. To assess the effectiveness of internal control

C
